name: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi
funding: Owned by Abu Dhabi's state-owned Tourism Development and Investment Company; the Guggenheim Foundation runs the programme. The Department of Culture and Tourism set the opening for 11 December 2026.
watch: Gulf Labor Coalition has campaigned for about 16 years, staged a 2014 protest at the New York Guggenheim and called for an artist boycott.
why_flagged: Owned by Abu Dhabi's state-owned Tourism Development and Investment Company; the Guggenheim Foundation runs the programme. The Department of Culture and Tourism set the opening for 11 December 2026.
records_note: Its site refused every page fetch, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; the project is run with Abu Dhabi's culture department.
other_findings: Democracy Now!, 2014-02-24: Gulf Labor activists dropped banners inside the New York Guggenheim over conditions for South Asian migrant workers building the Abu Dhabi museum. | Democracy Now!, 2015-04-02: The UAE barred NYU professor Andrew Ross, a Gulf Labor member pressing the Guggenheim over Saadiyat labour, from entering the country. | WikiLeaks, 2008-08 to 2010-01: US cables describe Guggenheim Abu Dhabi as a TDIC project and record the UAE rejecting Human Rights Watch's labour-abuse findings on Saadiyat. | WikiLeaks, 2010-10-12: An AFP report forwarded in Stratfor's emails says the Tourism Development and Investment Company, "a government body", invited contractors to bid for the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi on Saadiyat Island, due in 2013. The archive lists no email date. (news item forwarded in a leak)

name: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts
funding: Congress pays for the federally owned building; programmes run on ticket sales and private gifts. Trump became chair in February 2025; a $100M FY2026 revenue shortfall was projected.
watch: Trump fired the president and board in February 2025. Hamilton, Issa Rae, Renée Fleming and Philip Glass pulled out of the Center.
why_flagged: Congress pays for the federally owned building; programmes run on ticket sales and private gifts. Trump became chair in February 2025; a $100M FY2026 revenue shortfall was projected.
records_note: Its annual reports run 2017 to 2023 with financial reports for 2021 to 2023; Form 990s are on ProPublica; funders and board were not checked.
other_findings: Democracy Now!, 2025-03-31: After Trump made himself Kennedy Center chair in February, new leadership fired at least seven Social Impact staff, including artistic director Marc Bamuthi Joseph, who said the takeover is destroying a sanctuary for creative expression. | Democracy Now!, 2025-12-19: The Kennedy Center board, hand-picked by Trump after he named himself chair, voted to rename the venue for Trump and Kennedy. Democratic lawmakers said any name change needs an act of Congress. | Democracy Now!, 2026-06-01: Judge Christopher Cooper ruled Trump's rebranding of the Kennedy Center illegal and temporarily barred its closure. Trump had announced a two-year closure after a wave of artists and performers resigned or canceled. | Democracy Now!, 2026-09-16: Trump's Kennedy Center board voted to close the center immediately, citing financial shortages and renovations, hours after a judge again blocked adding Trump's name without congressional approval. | Democracy Now!, 2026-06-16: Dozens of artists and organizations, including the San Francisco Ballet and the Martha Graham Dance Company, pulled out of Kennedy Center performances after Trump appointed himself chair. Fired programmer Mallory Miller co-founded Hands Off the Arts. | Democracy Now!, 2025-03-10: Drag performers led a protest outside the Kennedy Center against Trump's takeover. Organizer Lord Henry demanded the board reinstate queer programming after Trump fired the president, replaced the board and named himself chairman.

name: National Museum of American History (Smithsonian)
funding: A Smithsonian museum. About two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money comes from Congress; the rest is private gifts, endowment and earned income.
watch: In August 2025 the museum removed a reference to Trump's two impeachments from its presidency exhibit, and the White House put it under content review.
why_flagged: A Smithsonian museum. About two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money comes from Congress; the rest is private gifts, endowment and earned income.
records_note: No records of its own: parent Smithsonian posts a 2025 annual report naming donors, audited statements for 2011 to 2025, and 17 Regents.
other_findings: Democracy Now!, 2025-08-13: Democracy Now!, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported a White House plan for a far-reaching review of Smithsonian exhibitions to align them with Trump's interpretation of U.S. history. It followed the removal of references to his impeachments. | Democracy Now!, 2025-08-01: The National Museum of American History removed references to Trump's two impeachments from an exhibit. A person told the Washington Post the review came under White House pressure to remove an art museum director; the museum said the label was temporary.

name: National Museum of Natural History (Smithsonian)
funding: A Smithsonian museum; Congress supplies about two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money. David H. Koch, a board member, backed the Hall of Human Origins, which carries his name.
watch: The White House named it in its August 2025 content review. In 2015, 15 groups campaigned to remove Koch from the board.
why_flagged: A Smithsonian museum; Congress supplies about two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money. David H. Koch, a board member, backed the Hall of Human Origins, which carries his name.
records_note: No records of its own: parent Smithsonian posts a 2025 annual report naming donors, audited statements for 2011 to 2025, and 17 Regents.
other_findings: Democracy Now!, 2025-08-13: Democracy Now!, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported a White House plan for a far-reaching review of Smithsonian exhibitions to align them with Trump's interpretation of U.S. history. It followed the removal of references to his impeachments. | Democracy Now!, 2015-03-26: Democracy Now! reported scientists' call for museums to cut ties with Koch money. It said David Koch sat on the Smithsonian natural history museum's board and that a Koch-backed Smithsonian installation drew criticism. | WikiLeaks, 2009-12-07 to 2010-08-23: The New Yorker profile quotes Joseph Romm of ClimateProgress saying the Koch-funded Hall of Human Origins "whitewashes the modern climate issue". A ThinkProgress item in a Podesta-archive email says Koch's donations will name a Smithsonian wing. (news item forwarded in a leak)

watch: Trump said in May 2025 he was firing director Kim Sajet, who then resigned. Amy Sherald cancelled her show in July 2025 over a painting.
why_flagged: A Smithsonian museum; Congress supplies about two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money, the rest from private gifts, endowment and earned income.
records_note: No records of its own: parent Smithsonian posts a 2025 annual report naming donors, audited statements for 2011 to 2025, and 17 Regents.

A WSJ column in Stratfor's emails also reports the removal. (news item forwarded in a leak)
